extracted.intended_audience: innovators, researchers, industry and academic teams, and nontraditional inventors seeking DARPA funding or partnership
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles and programmatic priorities DARPA uses to define, fund, and transition high-risk/high-payoff defense research and development; useful for teams preparing proposals or planning collaboration/transition pathways. Emphasizes transformational impact, proof-of-concept, transition potential, interdisciplinary approaches, and DARPA-specific funding vehicles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission alignment: create and prevent technological surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: The DARPA mission is to create and prevent technological surprise for our national security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals and programs should align with DARPA's core mission of producing or preventing strategic technological surprise in support of national security; projects that do not advance that mission are out of scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for transformational breakthroughs (not incremental advances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike other agencies, DARPA is not satisfied with incremental advances. We push transformational breakthroughs – innovations that not only solve current challenges but also establish the U.S. as the leading driver of strategic technological invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DARPA funds work intended to produce revolutionary concepts, foundational discoveries, or tactical innovations rather than small, incremental improvements. Proposals should emphasize step-change impact and long-term strategic advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on fundamental research to establish proof of concept
rubrics_metrics.description: DARPA programs focus on the fundamental research required to establish proof of concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should aim to establish feasibility and demonstrate core scientific/technical principles (proof of concept) as a primary objective; funding is targeted at moving concepts from possibility toward demonstrable capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Path to transition and implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Performer teams define the path for putting new technologies into use in service of our nation’s warfighters, and transition partners lead the work of implementation, technology transfer, and commercialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful efforts articulate clear transition strategies and identify partners (e.g., transition partners, implementers, commercializers) who will carry technologies toward fielding and adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary reach and probing across disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: Constantly probing for the next big thing, program managers reach across scientific and engineering disciplines to uncover new challenges and potential solutions at the seams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DARPA values cross-disciplinary approaches and research that leverages intersections between fields; proposals that bridge domains or apply methods from other disciplines are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program manager-led vision and bold leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Program managers define their programs, setting the course for research performers to deliver revolutionary concepts, foundational discoveries, and tactical innovations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs are driven by individual PMs who are expected to provide vision, tenacity, and leadership; proposers should expect PMs to shape scope and direction and demonstrate how their work fits the PM's defined objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement of diverse collaborators and nontraditional inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: We fuel an innovation ecosystem that engages academic, industry, and government partners. Challenges invite ideas from nontraditional inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DARPA encourages participation from a broad ecosystem (academia, industry, government, nontraditional actors). Proposals that bring novel teams or unconventional approaches may be favorably viewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of alternative contracting and funding vehicles
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative contracting vehicles allow DARPA to seize every opportunity to advance our mission. In addition to multi-year programs, our approach to funding includes Challenges, Seedlings, Explorations, and SBIR/STTR initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should select or be prepared for the funding vehicle appropriate to their stage and risk profile (e.g., prizes/challenges for crowd-sourced ideas, seedling awards for early-stage concepts, explorations for accelerated timelines, SBIR/STTR for small-business-led development).

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenges / prize competitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenges that invite ideas from nontraditional inventors, with prizes up to $10M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prize competitions are used to crowd in ideas and performers outside traditional communities; entrants should design approaches for rapid demonstration and clearly show how success criteria align with DARPA objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seedlings: de-risking very early-stage concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Seedlings that move concepts from “disbelief” to “mere doubt”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seedlings are intended to provide very early, small-scale funding to challenge assumptions and produce initial evidence to justify larger follow-on investments; proposals should be focused, high-risk/high-reward, and aimed at producing decisive early data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explorations: accelerate timeline from concept to award
rubrics_metrics.description: Explorations that accelerate the timeline from concept to award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploration mechanisms are intended to speed identification and selection of promising ideas; teams should be prepared for compressed schedules and rapid milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR initiatives as paths to new programs
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR/STTR initiatives can lead to new programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small business innovation programs are a route for companies to demonstrate capabilities and potentially transition into larger DARPA programs; proposals should emphasize commercialization/transition potential and technical novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on speed and enabling collaborators to 'succeed faster'
rubrics_metrics.description: By fostering a nurturing environment, we empower diverse collaborators to succeed faster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DARPA prizes pace — rapid progress, quick iteration, and fast movement from discovery to demonstration increase a project's attractiveness. Proposals should include realistic, time-compressed plans and milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-year programs to move technology from possibility to field-ready capability
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to multi-year programs focused on developing technology from possibility to field-ready capability...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DARPA supports longer-term efforts intended to mature technologies to operational readiness; proposers should show how multi-year funding will achieve field-relevant milestones and readiness for transition.
